description_en: Sarāḥ Phalcā, also known as Sadāvarta Phalcā, was originally built by the Sadāvarta Guṭhī of Śreṣṭhas from the Ikhāchẽ tola. It stands out for its remarkable pillar carvings.  Although no definitive evidence exists regarding the date of its initial construction, the wood carvings suggest that the pillars were erected during the late Malla period. The formerly L-shapedphalcāfeatured three bays facing east, five bays facing south, and one bay facing west.Local residents report that there were once statues of Umāmaheśvara, Nārāyaṇa and Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa on the rear wall, however, these statues have since disappeared. Many socio-cultural activities were historically performed in thephalcā, though many of these events are no longer practiced today. Until the early 2000s, a library was operated within thephalcā, but it has since closed, and its signboard has been removed.Sarāḥ Phalcā lost its roof in the 2015 earthquakes and remained covered by tarpaulins for several years. In November 2019, its side walls were dismantled to facilitate reconstruction. After a prolonged period of neglect the restoration of thephalcācommenced in 2022. In the 2022-2024 restoration, the floor plan was expanded to encompass the full width and length of the previously L-shaped building. Additionally, a second floor was added, topped with a flat, steel-reinforced concrete roof. Thus, the style (typology) of the building was transformed from aphalcato asataḥ.
description_ne: यो फल्चाको पुरानो नाम सदावर्त फल्चा हो । सदावर्त शब्द अपभ्रंश भएर सराः फल्चा नाम रहन गएको हो । इखाछेँ टोलका श्रेष्ठ परिवारले यो फल्चा बनाएको हो । ती श्रेष्ठहरूको सदावर्त गुठीबाट निर्माण गरेको हुनाले फल्चाको नाम सदावर्त फल्चा रहेको हो । मल्लकालीन प्रशासनमा महत्वपूर्ण स्थानमा रहेका ती श्रेष्ठहरू शक्तिशाली, सम्पन्न र प्रतिष्ठित थिए । फल्चा कुन मितिमा बनाएको भन्ने स्पष्ट पार्ने अभिलेख प्राप्त भएको छैन तर फल्चाको कलाकारिताबाट उत्तर-मध्यकालतिर निर्मांण गरेको स्पष्ट हुन्छ । यो फल्चा अंग्रेजी वर्णमालाको L अक्षरको स्वरूपमा बनाइएको छ । फल्चाको भित्तामा गवाक्ष बनाएर पश्चिमाभिमुख गरी उमामहेश्वरको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको थियो भने दक्षिणाभिमुख गरी नारायण र लक्ष्मीनारायणको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको थियो । तर अहिले ती मूर्तिहरू चोरी भइसकेका छन् ।पहिले यस फल्चामा निकै धेरै धार्मिक गतिविधि हुन्थे । प्रत्येक वर्ष माघ शुक्ल पुर्णिमा (सिपुन्हि) को दिनमा सदावर्त गुठीको तर्फबाट गाईलाई गहुँ खुवाउने परम्परा थियो । अहिले बाली आउन बन्द भएपनि गुठीका सदस्यहरूले आफ्नै खर्चमा गाईलाई गहुँ खुवाइरहेका छन् । प्रत्येक वर्ष इन्द्रजात्राको दिनमा फल्चामा बत्ती बाली समयबजि वितरण गरिनथ्यो । त्यस्तै प्रत्येक वर्ष रातो मच्छिन्द्रनाथ जात्रामा सुन्धाराबाट लगनखेल तान्ने छ्वय्‌लाभूको दिनमा समयबजि वितरण गरिन्थ्यो । हाल यी दुबै दिनमा समयबजि वितरण गर्ने प्रचलन बन्द भइसकेको छ । विसं २०५० सालतिर फल्चाको जीर्णोद्धार गरी इखाछेँ टोलमा रहेको आलोक पुस्तकालयलाई फल्चामा सारिएको थियो। विसं २०७२ को भूकम्पले फल्चामा क्षति पुगेकोले ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाको आर्थिक सहयोगमा फल्चाको मर्मतको काम भइरहेको छ ।

historical_events.event_name: Repair of the phalcā and establishment of a library
historical_events.event_description: The descendants of the donor family and other people repaired the Sarāḥ Phalcā and established the Aloka library of Ikhachen.
The building was severely damaged in the 2015 earthquakes. The roof was badly damaged and four corner struts collapsed. Three of them were preserved in the library, while one has been lost.

historical_events.event_name: Collection of funds for the restoration
historical_events.event_description: Lalitpur Metropolitan City office provided seven Lakh Rupees for the monument's reconstruction. The descendants of the donor family added fifty thousand Rupees, however, this amount was not sufficiet for the work to begin. The Metropolitan City office has promised to provide an additional three Lakh Rupees.

In the 2022-2024 restoration, the floor plan was expanded to encompass the full width and length of the previously L-shaped building. Additionally, a second floor was added, topped with a flat, steel-reinforced concrete roof. Thus, the style (typology) of the building was transformed from aphalcato asataḥ.
